description: Continuous Kerberos RC4 exposure tracking for Active Directory, built on Windows Security events 4768 and 4769 plus the Kdcsvc KDC events 201-209 from the System log, collected by Grafana Alloy into Loki. Answers who is still receiving RC4 tickets, which service accounts hold no AES key material, which clients advertise no AES, which ticket requests already fail with KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOTSUPP, and which domain controllers still advertise RC4, and what the KDC itself is warning about or already refusing - continuously, instead of as a point-in-time PowerShell export. Relevant to the RC4 deprecation tracked as CVE-2026-20833. Replace the YOUR LOGO placeholder in the header panel to brand it.

panels.title: RC4 Tickets Issued
panels.description: Tickets the KDC still encrypted with RC4 (0x17 / 0x18). Target is zero.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x17|0x18" [$__range]))

panels.title: Accounts Using RC4
panels.description: Distinct requesting accounts that received at least one RC4 ticket in range. Counting distinct values needs one series per account, so on a large estate at the start of remediation this can hit Loki max_query_series (500 by default). Narrow the range if it does.

targets.expr: count(sum by (account) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='TargetUserName'>(?P<account>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x17|0x18" [$__range])))

panels.title: Services Without AES Keys
panels.description: Distinct services whose Available Keys field holds no AES key material. Remediation is a password reset.

targets.expr: count(sum by (service) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "ServiceAvailableKeys" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceAvailableKeys'>(?P<svc_keys>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceName'>(?P<service>[^<]*)</Data>` | svc_keys!="" | svc_keys!="N/A" | svc_keys!="-" | svc_keys!~".*AES.*" [$__range])))

panels.title: ETYPE_NOTSUPP Failures
panels.description: Event 4769 with failure code 0xE - client and service could not agree an encryption type. These are already broken.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id="4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='Status'>(?P<status>[^<]*)</Data>` | status="0xe" [$__range]))

panels.title: AES Adoption
panels.description: Share of issued tickets using AES128 or AES256, out of all tickets that produced an encryption type. Target is 100%.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x11|0x12" [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype!="" | etype!="0xffffffff" [$__range])) * 100

panels.title: Domain Controllers Reporting
panels.description: Collection health. Compare against the number of DCs you expect to be shipping events - a drop here means blind spots, not good news.

targets.expr: count(sum by (computer) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} [$__range])))

options.content:
Why this exists
Microsoft is removing RC4 as the default supported encryption type for AD domain controllers (CVE-2026-20833), because an RC4 service ticket can be taken away and brute-forced offline. Enforcement landed with the July 2026 update.

The documented remediation path is a point-in-time PowerShell audit. A service account that authenticates once a month over RC4 is not in that snapshot, and it breaks the day enforcement lands. RC4 removal is a continuous monitoring problem.

Reading encryption types
0x12 AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96, good
0x11 AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96, good
0x17 RC4-HMAC, remove
0x18 RC4-HMAC-EXP, remove
0x1 / 0x3 DES, remove
0xffffffff no ticket issued (request failed)

Not the same thing as the msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes bitmask, where 0x18 means AES128 plus AES256, the opposite meaning.

Where the data comes from
A single stream: Windows Security events 4768 (TGT) and 4769 (service ticket), collected by Grafana Alloy and stored in Loki.

Since the November 2022 updates, these events carry ServiceAvailableKeys, ServiceSupportedEncryptionTypes, ClientAdvertizedEncryptionTypes and DCSupportedEncryptionTypes, enough to answer every question below from one datasource, with no agent on the clients and no scheduled script.

panels.title: Services Without AES Key Material - Remediation Worklist
panels.description: One row equals one account to fix. Available Keys with no AES entry means the account cannot negotiate AES at all. Remediation is a password reset to generate AES keys, then msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 24. An empty table is the healthy state.

targets.expr: topk(200, sum by (service, svc_keys, svc_set) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "ServiceAvailableKeys" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceAvailableKeys'>(?P<svc_keys>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceSupportedEncryptionTypes'>(?P<svc_set>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceName'>(?P<service>[^<]*)</Data>` | svc_keys!="" | svc_keys!="N/A" | svc_keys!="-" | svc_keys!~".*AES.*" [$__range])))

panels.title: Tickets by Encryption Family
panels.description: Stacked ticket volume by encryption family. The RC4 band reaching zero and staying there is the definition of done.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x11|0x12" [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x17|0x18" [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x1|0x3" [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype="0xffffffff" [$__interval]))

panels.title: RC4 Tickets by Domain Controller
panels.description: Which DCs are still serving RC4. Often a single site or one legacy application server is behind the whole number.

targets.expr: sum by (computer) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x17|0x18" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Clients Advertising No AES - The Fix Belongs On The Client
panels.description: The client machine advertised an encryption type list containing no AES. The service may already be AES-capable; the negotiation is being dragged down by the client. On Java and SAP hosts, look at krb5.ini.

targets.expr: topk(200, sum by (service, client_ip, client_etypes) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "ClientAdvertizedEncryptionTypes" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='ClientAdvertizedEncryptionTypes'>(?P<client_etypes>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceName'>(?P<service>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='IpAddress'>(?P<client_ip>[^<]*)</Data>` | client_etypes!="" | client_etypes!="-" | client_etypes!~".*AES.*" [$__range])))

options.content:
Remediation guide - one object at a time
No AES keys (Available Keys shows RC4 only): the account physically cannot do AES → reset the account password to generate AES key material. The password value does not have to change. Then set msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 24 (0x18).

Client negotiating RC4: the service already has AES; the listed client IPs advertise no AES → enable AES on those clients via GPO Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos. On Java and SAP hosts the cause is C:\Windows\krb5.ini carrying rc4-hmac in default_tkt_enctypes; the JVM reads it at startup, so restart the service after editing.

DC posture: once dependent objects are clean, set DefaultDomainSupportedEncTypes = 0x18 on the KDC. A service that genuinely needs RC4 gets a scoped msDS-SET = 0x1C (28, RC4 plus AES128 plus AES256) instead, which is the value Microsoft documents for a controlled rollback. Not 0x24: that is RC4 plus an AES256 session key and no AES long-term keys, which is not what you want on an account.

Failure signature after enforcement: KRB_AP_ERR 0xE KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOTSUPP, klist 0xc00002fd.

panels.title: Failing Now - KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOTSUPP (0xE)
panels.description: Already broken today. Invisible in the KDC audit events, and usually masked by an NTLM fallback that makes the application look healthy while silently downgrading the authentication.

targets.expr: topk(200, sum by (service, account, client_ip) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id="4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='Status'>(?P<status>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceName'>(?P<service>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='TargetUserName'>(?P<account>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='IpAddress'>(?P<client_ip>[^<]*)</Data>` | status="0xe" [$__range])))

panels.title: RC4 Tickets by Service, Account and Client
panels.description: Every RC4 ticket still being issued, attributed to the requesting account and the client IP that asked for it. This is the list you work down.

targets.expr: topk(200, sum by (service, account, client_ip, etype) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='ServiceName'>(?P<service>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='TargetUserName'>(?P<account>[^<]*)</Data>` | regexp `<Data Name='IpAddress'>(?P<client_ip>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x17|0x18" [$__range])))

panels.title: DCs Advertising RC4
panels.description: Domain controllers whose DCSupportedEncryptionTypes still includes RC4. Target after cleanup is 0x18 (AES only).

targets.expr: count(sum by (computer) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "DCSupportedEncryptionTypes" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='DCSupportedEncryptionTypes'>(?P<dc_set>[^<]*)</Data>` | dc_set!="-" | dc_set=~".*RC4.*" [$__range])))

panels.title: Ticket Events Collected
panels.description: Total 4768 / 4769 events ingested in range. A sudden drop usually means a broken bookmark or a stopped collector, not a quiet estate.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} [$__range]))

panels.title: Telemetry Ingested
panels.description: Bytes of Kerberos event data ingested in range. Watch this before widening the collection: the Security channel on a busy domain controller is measured in gigabytes a day, which is why the collector drops the rendered message.

targets.expr: sum(bytes_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} [$__range]))

panels.title: Pre-Auth Failures (4771)
panels.description: Kerberos pre-authentication failures. Not RC4-specific, but a spike here right after an enforcement change is the first symptom.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id="4771"} [$__range]))

panels.title: DC Encryption Posture - DCSupportedEncryptionTypes
panels.description: What each domain controller reports as its own supported encryption types, read straight from the ticket events. Anything containing RC4 or DES is a DC still advertising the weak ciphers.

targets.expr: sum by (computer, dc_set) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "DCSupportedEncryptionTypes" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='DCSupportedEncryptionTypes'>(?P<dc_set>[^<]*)</Data>` | dc_set!="" | dc_set!="-" [$__range]))

panels.title: Pre-Auth Failures by Domain Controller
panels.description: Event 4771 over time, per DC. Watch this during and after any encryption-type enforcement change.

targets.expr: sum by (computer) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id="4771"} [$__interval]))

panels.title: Requests Blocked by the KDC
panels.description: Events 203 / 204 / 208 / 209. The KDC refused to issue a ticket because of the RC4 policy. Every one of these is an authentication that failed, so this is the number that wakes people up.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", channel="System", event_id=~"203|204|208|209"} [$__range]))

panels.title: RC4 Dependencies Warned
panels.description: Events 201 / 202 / 206 / 207. The KDC still issued the ticket, but flagged the request as depending on RC4. This is your remediation backlog while the phase is still audit.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", channel="System", event_id=~"201|202|206|207"} [$__range]))

panels.title: DCs Reporting the Policy
panels.description: Domain controllers that emitted any 201-209 event in range. If this is lower than your DC count, the rest are either not collected or not running the disablement phase, and their silence means nothing.

targets.expr: count(sum by (computer) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", channel="System", event_id=~"20[1-9]"} [$__range])))

panels.title: Explicit RC4 in DDSET (205)
panels.description: Event 205. RC4 is explicitly enabled in the domain policy DefaultDomainSupportedEncTypes. A configuration finding rather than a failed request, which is why it is counted separately from the per-request warnings.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", channel="System", event_id="205"} [$__range]))

panels.title: KDC Events by ID
panels.description: Warnings and blocks over time. During a migration the shape you want is the warning bands falling to zero before you move the phase to enforcement, and the block bands never appearing at all.

targets.expr: sum by (event_id) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", channel="System", event_id=~"20[1-9]"} [$__interval]))

panels.title: KDC Verdict by Event and Domain Controller
panels.description: What each domain controller is reporting, decoded. Blocks in red are already failing. Warnings in orange are what will fail when the phase moves to enforcement.

201.text: 201 warn - client offers only RC4, no explicit config

202.text: 202 warn - service has no AES keys, no explicit config

204.text: 204 BLOCK - service without AES keys refused

205.text: 205 warn - RC4 explicitly enabled in DDSET policy

206.text: 206 warn - client offers only RC4, AES-only config

207.text: 207 warn - service has no AES keys, AES-only config

208.text: 208 BLOCK - RC4-only client refused, AES-only config

209.text: 209 BLOCK - no AES keys refused, AES-only config

targets.expr: sum by (event_id, computer) (count_over_time({job="$job", computer=~"$dc", channel="System", event_id=~"20[1-9]"} [$__range]))

panels.title: Raw RC4 Ticket Events
panels.description: The underlying events behind every number above, reduced to the event_data payload. Use this to confirm a finding before you touch an account.

targets.expr: {job="$job", computer=~"$dc", event_id=~"4768|4769"} |= "TicketEncryptionType" | json event_data="event_data" | line_format "{{.event_data}}" | regexp `<Data Name='TicketEncryptionType'>(?P<etype>[^<]*)</Data>` | etype=~"0x17|0x18"

panels.title: Raw KDC Events
panels.description: The Kdcsvc events with their rendered message, which is where the account and service names live. Empty here means the disablement phase is not emitting, so check RC4DefaultDisablementPhase before you conclude anything.

targets.expr: {job="$job", computer=~"$dc", channel="System", event_id=~"20[1-9]"}
